title: Inexact sequential quadratic programming methods for large-scale nonlinear optimization
contribution: PhD dissertation that introduces a matrix-free inexact line-search SQP method whose Krylov termination tests are derived from a penalty-model reduction (with separate primal and dual residual bounds), an inertia-tolerant step acceptance for negative curvature, and a flexible penalty function interpolating between a penalty function and a one-element filter, each with global first-order convergence and Matlab/KNITRO numerics.
problem_entry: Scale wall in PDE-constrained optimization where factorization is impractical (pp. 11, 22); inexact methods mature for unconstrained problems and equations but not constrained ones (p. 12); posed as how accurately the SQP subproblem must be solved to keep global convergence (p. 23); Ch. 6 enters via the blocking behaviour of penalties and filters (pp. 77-80).
key_idea: Accept an inexact primal-dual step when it reduces a local model of the exact penalty function, with primal and dual residuals bounded separately (Termination Tests I/II, pp. 26-29); accept a step before the inertia is corrected if computable curvature/normal-step tests hold (pp. 62-66); let the penalty parameter range over an interval [pi_l, pi_u] whose endpoints recover penalty and one-element filter (p. 82).
assumptions: Smooth equality-constrained problems; Assumptions 3.4: bounded functions/derivatives, bounded multipliers, uniformly full-rank Jacobians, bounded W, W positive definite on null(A) (p. 33), (b),(c) admitted strong (p. 33); Ch. 5 drops (e) except where inertia is correct (p. 67); scale-dependent beta admitted not ideal (p. 30).
proof_devices: analysis-only tangential/normal decomposition d = u + v, never computed (pp. 33-34)
case split K1/K2 by ||u||^2 >= gamma4 ||v||^2 with one progress measure Theta_k bounding step norm, directional derivative and steplength (Lemmas 3.7-3.10, pp. 36-39)
computable directional-derivative surrogate g'd - pi(||c|| - ||r||) usable in Armijo (Lemma 3.2, (3.10)-(3.11), pp. 31-32)
penalty boundedness by bounding model-reduction terms by (||c|| - ||r||) via bound (3.6b) (Lemma 3.11, pp. 39-42)
telescoping fixed-penalty merit decrease, then contraction recursion on the dual residual (Lemma 3.12, Theorem 3.13, pp. 42-45)
observable inequalities ||Ad||/||A|| <= ||v|| turning the implicit case split into explicit acceptance tests (Lemma 5.2, pp. 65-66; p. 67)
reuse of the Ch. 3 lemma chain for the flexible penalty, proving only the touched lemmas (Lemmas 6.3-6.6, pp. 90-94); constant-label slip in the Lemma 6.4 proof (p. 92)
experiments: Ch. 4: Matlab + unpreconditioned GMRES on 44 CUTEr/COPS problems kept if the exact-solve variant solved them (p. 50); baseline ires differing only in stopping rule, kappa = 2^-1..2^-9, 50-86 % vs 100 % solved (pp. 51-52); hybrid shows 0.5 extra GMRES iterations per run (pp. 52-53); PDE inverse problems, 27-point parameter grid, Jacobian mat-vecs as metric (pp. 53-58). Ch. 5: KNITRO-Direct, 36 problems with wrong inertia, iteration/factorization profiles (pp. 72-75). Ch. 6: KNITRO-Direct, 85 problems, iteration/function-evaluation profiles (pp. 94-97). Losses only in appendix tables (pp. 112, 114-115); no CPU times.
positioning: Corrects inexact Newton's whole-residual forcing for nonconvex constrained problems (pp. 23, 25); separates from composite-step inexact SQP (Heinkenschloss-Vicente etc.) and from full-space PDE methods lacking global guarantees (pp. 23-24, 26-27); penalty update from Waltz et al. (pp. 19, 30); even-handed critique of penalty and filter blocking (pp. 77-80).
writing: Repeated chapter arc motivation-algorithm-well-posedness-analysis-numerics-final remarks (pp. 7-8); explicit 'we claim' for argued statements (pp. 28, 48, 52, 84, 95, 99); geometric ||c||-f plane figures carry the globalization argument (pp. 18-19, 78-88); warm evaluative words with counter-cases left in appendices (pp. 73, 96).
limits_future: Strong assumptions (p. 33), no rate guarantee without a forcing sequence (p. 46), singular Jacobians not analyzed (p. 46), no preconditioner in CUTEr tests (p. 51), per-application tuning (p. 58), Ch. 5 needs the full step before testing (p. 76); future: inexact interior-point and flexible penalty in IPM and trust-region SQP (pp. 99-103), Ch. 5 tests in the inexact setting (pp. 75-76).

method_links.note: Earliest form: inner Krylov termination tests derived from the penalty-model reduction with separate primal/dual residuals; one-component baseline and deliberately naive failure tests already present; the dissertation reports 50-86 % for the baseline vs SKILL's 45-86 % from the 2008 paper (different version).
Penalty raised only when Test II signals feasibility progress; flexible-penalty update rules for pi_l and pi_u are the design object; filter criticised for needing a restoration backup.
Names the blocking effect as the main weakness of penalty methods, an early seed of the later penalty doubt (SKILL Inner Tension 3).
Rivals built in the same code differing in one component: ires (stopping rule), matmod (no (5.8)/(5.9)), pi_default (single penalty) in KNITRO-Direct.
Incumbent wins (e.g. orthrgds, eigenb2, eigenc2, elec3) appear only in appendix tables, not in the prose; PDE parameters chosen by a grid on the evaluation problems.
Hard instances selected by the hazard (problems where the inertia was wrong at least once), not mechanically constructed.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Flexible penalty function: pi_l = pi_u gives the penalty function, pi_l = 0 and pi_u = infinity a one-element filter; endpoint updates designed separately.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: make the proof's case split computable
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Analysis-only null/range decomposition and K1/K2 split (Ch. 3) turned into observable acceptance inequalities (5.8)/(5.9) in Ch. 5.
Test the current primal-dual solution for acceptability before another Hessian modification; argued even more valuable in an inexact setting.

transferable: Baseline = own solver with only the inner stopping rule replaced by the textbook relative-residual test, swept over kappa = 2^-1..2^-9, success rate per value (pp. 51-52, 109).
Price a safeguard with a hybrid run adding it to the baseline: extra inner iterations per run vs extra problems solved (pp. 52-53).
One progress measure Theta_k per step type bounding step norm, merit decrease and steplength at once, then telescope (pp. 36-42).
Replace an unobservable proof split by observable inequalities (||Ad||/||A|| lower-bounds the normal component) and add them to the algorithm (pp. 65-67).
Move the lower end of a parameter range toward the smallest value that would have accepted the step, by a fraction with a minimum increment (pp. 89, 95).
Use the operation the preconditioner consumes (Jacobian mat-vecs) as headline metric when iteration counts are uninformative (p. 57).
Draw the region each acceptance mechanism blocks in the ||c||-f plane to argue for a new one (pp. 78-88).
coauthors: none (single-author dissertation; advisor Jorge Nocedal; Richard Byrd acknowledged as essential, p. 5)

quotes.text: The main purpose of this chapter is to determine the accuracy with which the SQP subproblems must be solved in order to ensure global convergence in the context of a practical algorithm for problem (2.1).
A major theme in this work has been the importance of tying various aspects of the optimization process into one cohesive unit.
